title: The Man on Putney Hill
question: Today, can the narrator find a purpose worth living for in a beaten world?
light: low sun from the east, deep black shadows
palette: night blue, lamplight amber, gorse yellow, clay umber, red-weed violet, deep black

inn_bedroom_night.described: A small attic servant's bedroom at the top of the inn on Putney Hill at night. An iron bedstead with a made bed and grey blankets stands against the left wall under the sloping ceiling. A washstand with a chipped white jug stands at the right, two opened tins of pineapple and a gnawed crust of bread on its marble top. A rush chair sits beside the bed. A sash window in the right wall shows a dark road and a faint starlit sky. Cold blue starlight falls in from the sash window at the right and lays a pale square across the grey blankets, and the far corners sink into deep black shadow under the slope of the ceiling. Bare boards cover the floor. Grey daylight through the window at the LEFT, deep shadow.
inn_bedroom_night.route: from the iron bedstead at the left across the bare boards to the sash window at the right
inn_bedroom_night.geometry: In the establishing wide the iron bedstead fills the LEFT half of the frame, its foot rail along the BOTTOM edge and its head rail a third of the frame's height. The sash window stands in the RIGHT third, its top near the TOP edge under the sloping ceiling, a quarter of the frame's width. The washstand stands beneath the window at the RIGHT edge, half the bedstead's height, and the rush chair sits at CENTRE between washstand and bed.
inn_bedroom_night.ambience: a night breeze at the sash, a loose slate ticking on the roof, a distant dog barking

common_edge_morning.described: The verge of Wimbledon Common at sunrise. A swampy hollow of rushes and brown shallow water lies at the lower left among birch trunks, little brown frogs swarming on the mud, a fallen birch log lying across the water. Ten yards beyond it, at the right, a dense clump of dark holly and bramble bushes stands head high, a shadowed trodden opening at its base. Rough grass, heather, yellow gorse and broom spread around it, birch and oak trees behind. Low golden sun rises from the LEFT, out of the east, and throws long shadows of the birches across the grass toward the right, dew sparkling on the bramble leaves. Above hangs a pink sky fretted with little golden clouds.
common_edge_morning.route: from the swampy hollow of rushes at the near left across the rough grass to the holly and bramble clump at the far right
common_edge_morning.geometry: In the establishing wide the swampy hollow occupies the LEFT third along the BOTTOM edge, the fallen birch log a fifth of the frame's width across its water. The holly and bramble clump stands in the RIGHT half, its top at half the frame's height, its dark opening at the BOTTOM of the right third. Birch trunks rise to the TOP edge between them at CENTRE, gorse in yellow patches across the middle distance, and the pink sky fills the top quarter.
common_edge_morning.ambience: frogs croaking in the rushes, larks over the heath, wind in the birches, a single rook calling

bower_morning.described: A little bower inside a dense clump of holly and bramble bushes on Wimbledon Common, a hollow of flattened dry grass with room for two to sit. Arching branches curve across the top of the hollow and close it on three sides. Dead holly leaves lie on the grass, and a bramble stem arches across the top of the hollow. Through a gap in the leaves at the right, far off, a hazy view of London's roofs runs along the horizon under a faint smudge of grey smoke. The bower's mouth opens low at the left onto rough grass and gorse. Low morning sunlight slants in sideways from the RIGHT through the leaf gap, laying bright coins on the grass inside the green shade and throwing the branch shadows long toward the LEFT, with deep black shadow in the far corners.
bower_morning.landmark: the gap in the leaves showing London
bower_morning.route: from the low bower mouth at the left across the flattened grass to the seat beneath the leaf gap at the right
bower_morning.geometry: In the establishing wide the flattened grass floor fills the BOTTOM third edge to edge. The arching branches frame the TOP edge and both side edges, dark holly a fifth of the frame deep on each side. The gap in the leaves opens in the RIGHT third at half the frame's height, the London roofs inside it a thin band a tenth of the frame tall. The low mouth of the bower opens at the LEFT edge, a quarter of the frame's height.
bower_morning.ambience: bees in the bramble, wind stirring the holly leaves, a far rook, a faint deep rumble from London

cellar_digging_day.described: A brick-vaulted coal cellar beneath the kitchen wing of a stucco villa on Putney Hill, about twelve by sixteen feet, with an earth floor. In the far wall a dark rough burrow mouth about four feet high is cut through the brick footing into yellow clay, shored with a few planks. A heap of fresh yellow clay spoil and a wooden garden barrow stand beside it, two spades leaning on the brick. At the left a heap of coal lies under the chute hatch. Wine bins line the right wall. Grey daylight falls in from the pavement grating above the coal chute at the left, laying a pale shaft across the earth floor, and the corners of the vault stay in deep brown shadow. Raking grey daylight from the LEFT, deep shadow.
cellar_digging_day.route: from the foot of the kitchen steps at the near edge across the earth floor to the burrow mouth in the far wall
cellar_digging_day.geometry: In the establishing wide the burrow mouth sits at CENTRE in the far wall, a quarter of the frame's height, its planks framing it. The clay spoil heap and the garden barrow stand at its right, half its height. The coal heap and the grating shaft fill the LEFT third, the shaft falling from the TOP edge. The wine bins run up the RIGHT edge to the vault, and the earth floor fills the BOTTOM third.
cellar_digging_day.ambience: spades biting clay, a barrow wheel squeaking, water dripping in the vault, muffled birdsong through the grating

cellar_cards_night.described: The same brick-vaulted coal cellar at night, seen toward its west wall. A plain deal kitchen table with two kitchen chairs stands at centre under a hanging oil lamp. Scattered playing cards, a chessboard with its chessmen, a champagne bottle, two glasses and cigar ash in a saucer cover the table top. Behind it wooden wine bins hold dusty bottles of champagne and burgundy. Stone steps rise at the left toward a closed kitchen door. The single hanging oil lamp throws warm amber light down from above the table, and the curve of the vault and the corners behind the bins fall into deep black shadow.
cellar_cards_night.route: from the deal table under the oil lamp across the earth floor to the stone steps rising at the left
cellar_cards_night.geometry: In the establishing wide the deal table stands at CENTRE, half the frame's width, its top at the frame's lower third line. The hanging oil lamp hangs at the TOP centre, a tenth of the frame's height. The wine bins fill the back wall from the RIGHT edge to centre, two thirds of the frame's height. The stone steps rise from the BOTTOM left corner toward the closed kitchen door at the LEFT edge.
cellar_cards_night.ambience: the oil lamp hissing, cards slapping on deal, a cork popping, a drip in the vault

roof_night.described: The lead flat behind a brick parapet on the roof of a stucco villa on Putney Hill, at night. Slate slopes and a small dormer roof door stand at the near left, the top of a ladder showing in its opening. The brick parapet runs waist high across the lower third. Beyond it the London valley lies black to the northern hills. Fires near Kensington glow red at the far right with orange tongues of flame. Nearer, low ground shines with a pale violet-purple glow from the red weed, quivering in the night breeze. Mars burns red and clear high in the upper left, the western sky. The red light of a fire near Kensington falls in from the RIGHT across the roof and throws the parapet's shadow over the lead toward the LEFT in deep black. Pale moonlight falls from the upper RIGHT onto the wet slates, and the dormer door at the left sinks into black shadow.
roof_night.route: from the dormer roof door at the near left along the lead flat to the brick parapet at the right
roof_night.geometry: In the establishing wide the brick parapet runs from the LEFT edge to the RIGHT edge across the lower third, a sixth of the frame's height. The dormer roof door stands at the LEFT edge, a third of the frame's height. The black valley fills the middle band, the violet glow a wide streak at CENTRE, the red fires a small cluster at the RIGHT third. Mars is a red point in the TOP left quarter.
roof_night.ambience: a night breeze over the slates, a far crackle of fires toward Kensington, a distant dog barking

shots.frame: Medium of the narrator (grey eyes, sixteen days of grey-brown beard) standing at the sash window in the RIGHT third of the attic, peering down at the dark road.
shots.motion: The camera pushes in a hand's breadth toward the narrator at the sash window across the whole shot; his hand draws the sash an inch upward; his head turns along the dark road below.
shots.camera: Standing at the foot of the iron bedstead, chest height, three yards from the window, a 50mm lens; cold starlight comes from the RIGHT through the sash.
shots.at_rest: THE FOCUS OF THE PICTURE IS the narrator at the sash window in the RIGHT third, his body half the frame's height, one hand on the sash frame. The washstand with its chipped white jug stands beneath the window at the RIGHT edge, and the sloping ceiling fills the TOP edge in deep black shadow.
shots.end: The narrator fills the RIGHT half at the sash window, the sash raised an inch, his face turned down toward the dark road, the chipped jug at the BOTTOM right edge, starlight on his cheek.
source: prowled from window to window, peering out for some sign of these monsters
I lit no lamps, fearing some Martian might come beating that part of London for food in the night
shots.turn: hidden and safe -> watching for monsters
shots.why: Opens on a hunted man in a stolen room, fed but afraid to light a lamp; he is a watcher.

shots.frame: Insert of two opened tins of pineapple and a gnawed crust of bread on the marble top of the washstand.
shots.motion: The camera tracks sideways to the right past the chipped white jug across the whole shot, with the tins of pineapple behind it; the night breeze through the sash stirs the crumbs on the marble; loose crumbs roll along the marble toward its edge.
shots.camera: Standing at the washstand's left end, at tabletop height, two feet off, a 50mm lens; starlight falls from the RIGHT through the sash.
shots.at_rest: THE FOCUS OF THE PICTURE IS the two opened tins of pineapple at CENTRE on the marble top, the gnawed crust of bread lying at their left. The chipped white jug stands at the LEFT edge in the foreground, and the bottom of the sash window glows pale along the TOP edge.
shots.end: The two tins of pineapple stand in the LEFT third, the gnawed crust beside them, the sash window's pale square at the TOP right, and the marble top runs out to the RIGHT edge.
source: I found a rat-gnawed crust and two tins of pineapple
The place had been already searched and emptied.
shots.turn: starving -> fed on scraps
shots.why: The ransacked city has left him a rat's leavings; his whole world is now food and hiding.

shots.frame: Medium close of the narrator (grey eyes, sixteen days of grey-brown beard) sitting up in the iron bedstead, hands clasped at his chin, praying aloud to the dark.
shots.motion: The camera holds a locked-off frame; the narrator presses his clasped hands to his chin and prays aloud; his head bows toward his clasped hands.
shots.camera: Standing at the bedside, seated height, a yard off, a 50mm lens; cold starlight comes from the RIGHT across the grey blankets.
shots.at_rest: THE FOCUS OF THE PICTURE IS the narrator's clasped hands against his chin at CENTRE, his head a third of the frame's height, his grey eyes wide on the dark. The grey blankets fold across the BOTTOM edge, and the iron head rail runs behind him at the LEFT edge in deep black shadow.
shots.end: The narrator sits upright at CENTRE, his head a third of the frame's height bowed toward his clasped hands, the grey blankets across the BOTTOM edge, the iron head rail at the LEFT edge in deep black shadow.
source: I found myself sitting up in bed, staring at the dark.
I found myself praying that the Heat-Ray might have suddenly and painlessly struck her out of being.
shots.turn: numb -> praying in earnest
shots.why: His mind clears and turns on the curate, the Martians and his wife; he prays aloud for her a painless death.

shots.frame: Medium of the narrator (grey eyes, battered brown felt hat) bent low beside the rush chair, crossing the bare boards toward the sash window at first dawn, his trouser pockets bulging with biscuits.
shots.motion: The camera tracks beside the narrator as he walks bent low toward the sash window across the whole shot; he passes the rush chair; his hand pushes the sash upward.
shots.camera: Standing at the left wall beside the bedstead, chest height, two yards off, a 35mm lens; pale grey dawn light comes from the RIGHT through the sash.
shots.at_rest: THE FOCUS OF THE PICTURE IS the narrator bent low in the LEFT third beside the rush chair, his head and shoulders a quarter of the frame's height, both trouser pockets bulging with biscuits. The sash window glows pale grey in the RIGHT third, and the washstand with its chipped jug stands beneath it at the RIGHT edge.
shots.end: The narrator stands bent at the sash window in the RIGHT half, one hand pushing the raised sash, his pockets bulging, the rush chair behind him at the LEFT edge, pale dawn on his beard.
source: so soon as dawn had come
crept out of the house like a rat leaving its hiding place
shots.turn: a man who talked with God -> a rat leaving its hole
shots.why: Dawn shrinks him again: the praying man goes out like vermin under the masters' eyes.

shots.frame: Wide of the verge of Wimbledon Common, the narrator (grey eyes, battered brown felt hat) small beside the swampy hollow at the LEFT, the holly and bramble clump across the grass at the RIGHT.
shots.motion: The camera rises above the narrator at the swampy hollow across the whole shot, looking down over the common to the holly and bramble clump; the narrator bends toward the water; the low sun spreads gold across the gorse.
shots.camera: Standing in the rough grass at the edge of the birch trees, head height, twenty yards off, a 28mm lens; the low golden sun comes from the LEFT.
shots.at_rest: THE FOCUS OF THE PICTURE IS the narrator standing at the swampy hollow in the LEFT third, his body a fifth of the frame's height, looking down at the brown water. The fallen birch log crosses the water at the BOTTOM edge, and the dark holly and bramble clump stands in the RIGHT half, its opening in shadow.
shots.end: High wide over the common: the swampy hollow small at the BOTTOM left with the narrator bent over it, gorse patches gold across the CENTRE, the holly and bramble clump dark in the RIGHT third, the pink sky along the TOP edge.
source: In the road that runs from the top of Putney Hill to Wimbledon was a number of poor vestiges of the panic torrent
From the corner I went, under cover of a thicket of trees and bushes, to the edge of Wimbledon Common, stretching wide and far
shots.turn: lost on the wrecked road -> alone at the open common
shots.why: After the wreck of the flight along the road, the wide heath shows how alone he is.

shots.frame: Insert of little brown frogs swarming over the mud and rushes of the swampy hollow around the fallen birch log.
shots.motion: The camera pulls back from the log, travelling a forearm, across the whole shot; the little frogs push through the rushes and leap into the brown water; ripples run outward across the hollow.
shots.camera: Standing at the water's edge, knee height, a yard off, a 50mm lens; low golden sun from the LEFT through the birch trunks.
shots.at_rest: THE FOCUS OF THE PICTURE IS a cluster of little brown frogs on the mud at CENTRE beside the fallen birch log. Green rushes rise along the LEFT edge, the brown shallow water fills the BOTTOM third, and the log runs out of frame at the RIGHT edge in golden light.
shots.end: Fresh rings of ripples cover the brown water in the BOTTOM half, a few frogs on the birch log at the RIGHT, green rushes along the LEFT edge, the mud at CENTRE half empty.
source: I came upon a busy swarm of little frogs in a swampy place among the trees
drawing a lesson from their stout resolve to live
shots.turn: despair -> a lesson in resolve
shots.why: The frogs' stout will to live is the first answer the morning gives him.

shots.frame: Full of the artilleryman (Square weather-browned face, red cut across the chin and jaw) rising out of the shadowed opening at the base of the holly and bramble clump, Cutlass in hand.
shots.motion: The camera tracks behind the artilleryman, travelling two strides, across the whole shot; the artilleryman rises to his full height with the cutlass raised; his chest heaves with each hoarse breath.
shots.camera: Standing in the rough grass ten yards from the clump, knee height, a 50mm lens; the low sun comes from the LEFT and lays long birch shadows across the grass.
shots.at_rest: THE FOCUS OF THE PICTURE IS the artilleryman crouched in the dark opening at the BOTTOM of the clump at CENTRE, his crouched body a third of the frame's height, the cutlass blade across his knees. The holly leaves glisten with dew around him, the clump's dark top rises to the TOP edge, and yellow gorse glows at the LEFT edge.
shots.end: The artilleryman stands upright at CENTRE before the holly clump, his body three quarters of the frame's height, the cutlass raised at his right hip, the clump's dark top at the TOP edge, gorse at the LEFT edge.
source: I beheld something crouching amid a clump of bushes
it rose up and became a man armed with a cutlass
shots.turn: watched by something -> faced by an armed man
shots.why: The feeling of being watched becomes a man; the narrator's solitude breaks.

shots.frame: Medium close past the shoulder and back of the head of the narrator (battered brown felt hat, Cream-and-blue striped flannel shirt torn at the shoulder) toward the artilleryman (Square weather-browned face, red cut across the chin and jaw) shouting at him.
shots.motion: The camera holds over the narrator's shoulder toward the artilleryman across the whole shot; the artilleryman thrusts the cutlass forward and shouts; his free arm waves the narrator back.
shots.camera: Standing behind the narrator's right shoulder, eye height, four yards from the artilleryman, an 85mm lens; the low sun comes from the LEFT across the artilleryman's face.
shots.at_rest: THE FOCUS OF THE PICTURE IS the artilleryman's face in the RIGHT third, his head a third of the frame's height, black hair over his brows, the cutlass raised at his shoulder. The narrator's shoulder and the back of his felt hat fill the LEFT edge, and the holly clump stands dark behind along the TOP.
shots.end: The artilleryman stands in the RIGHT third, the cutlass point thrust toward the LEFT, his mouth open in a shout, the narrator's shoulder and hat brim at the LEFT edge, the holly dark along the TOP edge.
source: he cried, when I was within ten yards of him, and I stopped
Where do you come from?
shots.turn: approaching -> halted at ten yards
shots.why: The stranger claims the ground as his and the food for one: another man is a rival now.

shots.frame: One single picture fills the whole frame edge to edge. Each person in the picture is a different man with his own face, build and dress. Each person in the picture appears exactly once, with a face, hair and dress all his own. Medium close of the artilleryman (Square weather-browned face, red cut across the chin and jaw) seated beneath the leaf gap inside the bower, speaking.
shots.motion: The camera pushes in a hand's breadth toward the artilleryman's face across the whole shot; he counts on his thick fingers and speaks; his raised hand lifts toward the leaf gap above him.
shots.camera: Seated on the grass two yards in front of him, the lens level with his face, a 50mm lens; morning sun slants in from the RIGHT through the leaf gap.
shots.at_rest: THE FOCUS OF THE PICTURE IS the artilleryman's face at CENTRE, his head a third of the frame's height, black hair over his brows, the cutlass lying across his knees at the BOTTOM edge. The leaf gap with its hazy London roofs glows at the TOP right, and dark holly fills the LEFT edge.
shots.end: The artilleryman's face fills the CENTRE, his head half the frame's height, his raised hand at the TOP right before the leaf gap, the hazy roofs behind it, holly at the LEFT edge.
source: I believe they’ve built a flying-machine, and are learning to fly.
I went on into a little bower, and sat down.
shots.turn: safe in hiding -> the Martians may fly
shots.why: Old acquaintances hide together, and the soldier's first news is worse than any: the Martians are learning to fly.

shots.frame: Only the named people stand in the picture and everything else is the place. Each person in the picture is a different man with his own face, build and dress. Each person in the picture appears exactly once, with a face, hair and dress all his own. One single picture fills the whole frame edge to edge. Close of the artilleryman (Square weather-browned face, red cut across the chin and jaw) speaking under the arching holly.
shots.motion: The camera holds a locked-off frame across the whole shot; the artilleryman leans toward the lens and speaks; his head shakes from side to side.
shots.camera: Seated on the grass a yard in front of him, eye height, an 85mm lens; spots of sun fall in from the leaf gap at the RIGHT across his brow.
shots.at_rest: THE FOCUS OF THE PICTURE IS the artilleryman's face at CENTRE, his head half the frame's height, black hair falling over his eyes, the red cut across his chin. Dark holly leaves fill the LEFT edge, and the leaf gap with its hazy London roofs glows at the TOP right.
shots.end: The artilleryman's face fills the CENTRE, leaning a hand's breadth nearer, his head half the frame's height, the hazy roofs at the TOP right, holly at the LEFT edge, his jaw set hard.
source: I am. We’re down; we’re beat.
They carried absolute conviction.
shots.turn: a vague hope -> we are beaten
shots.why: The common soldier says aloud what the philosopher had refused to see.

shots.frame: Medium close of the narrator (grey eyes, sixteen days of grey-brown beard) sitting upright cross-legged inside the bower, staring before him.
shots.motion: The camera pulls back from the narrator's face across the whole shot, widening to show the arching holly and the bower's low mouth; his eyes drop to the grass; his hand works along his grey-brown beard.
shots.camera: Crouched two yards in front of him, the lens level with his face, a 50mm lens; sunlight falls in from the leaf gap at the RIGHT.
shots.at_rest: THE FOCUS OF THE PICTURE IS the narrator's face at CENTRE, his head a third of the frame's height, his grey eyes fixed past the lens, his shoulders upright. Arching holly branches frame the TOP edge, a bright coin of sunlight lies on the grass at the BOTTOM left, and the bower's low mouth glows at the LEFT edge.
shots.end: Medium of the narrator sitting upright at CENTRE, his head a fifth of the frame's height, his hand at his beard, the arching holly along the TOP edge, the bower's low mouth bright at the LEFT edge.
source: I sat staring before me, trying in vain to devise some countervailing thought.
That’s what we are now—just ants.
shots.turn: a lifelong habit of hope -> just ants
shots.why: He searches for a counter-thought and finds none; men are ants, and eatable ones.

shots.frame: Medium of the artilleryman (Square weather-browned face, brown civilian tweed waistcoat) seated beneath the leaf gap, pointing out through the leaves toward the London roofs.
shots.motion: The camera tilts up from the third to the smoke, travelling two strides, across the whole shot; his hand sweeps along the line of roofs; the wind carries the grey smoke along the horizon.
shots.camera: Seated on the grass three yards from him, eye height, a 35mm lens; morning sun slants in from the RIGHT through the leaf gap.
shots.at_rest: THE FOCUS OF THE PICTURE IS the artilleryman's pointing hand in the LEFT third, his seated body half the frame's height, his eyes shining. The leaf gap opens in the RIGHT third at half the frame's height, the hazy London roofs a thin band inside it under a smudge of grey smoke.
shots.end: The leaf gap fills the CENTRE, the hazy London roofs a band across it under grey smoke, the artilleryman's pointing fingertip at the LEFT edge, holly leaves framing the TOP and RIGHT edges.
source: I mean that men like me are going on living—for the sake of the breed.
I’m going on, under their feet.
shots.turn: beaten -> grim set on living
shots.why: The beaten man turns out to have a will: he means to go on, under their feet, for the sake of the breed.

shots.frame: Medium close of the narrator (grey eyes, sixteen days of grey-brown beard) gripping the hand of the artilleryman (Square weather-browned face, red cut across the chin and jaw) across the bower.
shots.motion: The camera holds a locked-off frame across the whole shot; the narrator grips the artilleryman's hand and cries out to him; their two joined hands pump up and down between them.
shots.camera: Seated on the grass beside them, chest height, two yards off, a 50mm lens; sun spots fall in from the leaf gap at the RIGHT.
shots.at_rest: THE FOCUS OF THE PICTURE IS the two clasped hands at CENTRE. The narrator kneels nearer in the LEFT third, his head a third of the frame's height. The artilleryman sits further back in the RIGHT third, his head a quarter of the frame's height, his eyes shining under black hair. Holly arches along the TOP edge.
shots.end: The clasped hands hold the CENTRE, the narrator's face turned three quarters to the lens in the LEFT third, his head a third of the frame's height, the artilleryman's grinning face in the RIGHT third, holly along the TOP edge.
source: I stared, astonished, and stirred profoundly by the man’s resolution.
And suddenly I gripped his hand.
I believed unhesitatingly both in his forecast of human destiny
shots.turn: doubt -> the narrator chooses the soldier's plan
shots.why: The philosopher submits to the soldier and takes his purpose as his own.

shots.frame: Full of the artilleryman (Square weather-browned face, brown civilian tweed waistcoat) digging at the burrow mouth while the narrator (battered brown felt hat, Cream-and-blue striped flannel shirt torn at the shoulder) wheels the garden barrow of clay across the earth floor.
shots.motion: The camera tracks sideways to the left past the clay spoil heap across the whole shot, with the artilleryman at the burrow mouth behind it; the artilleryman heaves a spadeful of clay into the barrow; the narrator pushes the barrow along toward the coal heap.
shots.camera: Standing by the wine bins at the right wall, chest height, five yards from the burrow, a 35mm lens; grey daylight falls from the grating at the LEFT.
shots.at_rest: THE FOCUS OF THE PICTURE IS the artilleryman at the burrow mouth at CENTRE, his body half the frame's height, the spade driven into yellow clay. The narrator stands nearer in the LEFT third behind the garden barrow, his body three quarters of the frame's height, and the clay spoil heap rises in the foreground at the RIGHT edge.
shots.end: The clay spoil heap passes out at the RIGHT edge, the artilleryman digging at CENTRE in the burrow mouth, the narrator wheeling the loaded barrow into the grey shaft of daylight in the LEFT third.

sounds.sound: a spade biting into wet clay

source: it was a burrow scarcely ten yards long
I had my first inkling of the gulf between his dreams and his powers
We had a garden barrow and shot the earth we removed against the kitchen range.
shots.turn: a grand scheme -> a ten-yard hole
shots.why: The purpose meets the spade: a week's work he could dig in a day, yet he is glad to labour.

shots.frame: Medium close of the artilleryman (Square weather-browned face, Full black moustache) at the deal table under the oil lamp, raising a champagne bottle as its cork flies.
shots.motion: The camera pushes in a hand's breadth toward the artilleryman's face across the whole shot; his thumb pops the cork and foam spills over his knuckles; he lifts the bottle high beside his cheek and calls out.
shots.camera: Seated across the deal table, chest height, a yard and a half off, a 50mm lens; the hanging oil lamp throws amber light down from the TOP.
shots.at_rest: THE FOCUS OF THE PICTURE IS the champagne bottle in the artilleryman's fist at the BOTTOM centre, his thumb at the cork. His face sits above it in the TOP third, his head a third of the frame's height, grinning under the amber lamplight, and the wine bins rise behind him at the RIGHT edge.
shots.end: The artilleryman's grinning face fills the CENTRE, his head half the frame's height, the foaming bottle raised beside his cheek in the RIGHT third, the oil lamp glowing at the TOP edge, the wine bins dark behind.
source: Neither of us seemed disposed to resume digging
I am host today. Champagne!
shots.turn: work to do -> a holiday declared
shots.why: The regenerator of the species calls a holiday; the plan gives way to the cellar's wine.

shots.frame: Insert of the chessboard with its chessmen, scattered playing cards, two glasses and a saucer with a smouldering cigar on the deal table under the hanging oil lamp.
shots.motion: The camera rises above the chessboard across the whole shot, looking down over the scattered cards and the two glasses; the lamp flame flickers in the draught from the stone steps; a thread of smoke rises from the cigar in the saucer.
shots.camera: Standing at the table's edge, tabletop height, a foot off, a 50mm lens; the oil lamp throws amber light down from the TOP.
shots.at_rest: THE FOCUS OF THE PICTURE IS the chessboard at CENTRE, a white king lying on its side among the chessmen. Scattered playing cards fan across the LEFT third, two champagne glasses and a saucer with a smouldering cigar stand at the RIGHT edge, and the amber pool of lamplight covers the BOTTOM half of the deal.
shots.end: Top-down over the deal table: the chessboard small at CENTRE, the fanned cards across the LEFT third, two glasses and the saucer at the RIGHT, a thread of cigar smoke crossing the TOP edge.
source: He taught me euchre, and after dividing London between us
Afterwards he taught me poker, and I beat him at three tough chess games.
shots.turn: the end of the species -> parish points
shots.why: Euchre, poker and chess fill the hours meant for the tunnel.

shots.frame: Medium of the narrator (grey eyes, battered brown felt hat) at the deal table laying down playing cards, the artilleryman (Square weather-browned face, brown civilian tweed waistcoat) across from him dealing.
shots.motion: The camera pulls back from the fan of cards in the narrator's hands across the whole shot, widening to show the whole deal table under the hanging oil lamp; the narrator slaps a card down on the deal; the artilleryman laughs and deals again.
shots.camera: Standing at the table's end beside the stone steps, chest height, two yards off, a 35mm lens; the oil lamp throws amber light down from the TOP.
shots.at_rest: THE FOCUS OF THE PICTURE IS the fan of playing cards in the narrator's hands in the LEFT third, his head a quarter of the frame's height. The artilleryman sits further back in the RIGHT third, his head a fifth of the frame's height, dealing, and the wine bins rise dark behind him.
shots.end: The deal table at CENTRE under the hanging oil lamp, the narrator at the LEFT laying a card, the artilleryman at the RIGHT dealing, the wine bins filling the back wall, the stone steps at the LEFT edge.
shots.changed: the lamp and table come in
source: Strange mind of man!
When dark came we decided to take the risk, and lit a lamp.
shots.turn: remorse set aside -> vivid delight in the game
shots.why: With the species at the edge of extermination, he finds the cards extremely interesting: the purpose has become a game.

shots.frame: Medium close of the narrator (grey eyes, sixteen days of grey-brown beard) at the deal table, a cigar between his fingers, looking up at the stone steps.
shots.motion: The camera pushes in toward the narrator's face in the RIGHT; the narrator draws on the cigar and lifts his eyes to the stone steps; the smoke curls up through the amber lamplight.
shots.camera: Standing beside the wine bins, chest height, a yard and a half off, a 50mm lens; the oil lamp throws amber light down from the TOP across his brow.
shots.at_rest: THE FOCUS OF THE PICTURE IS the narrator's face in the RIGHT third, his head a third of the frame's height, a lit cigar in his fingers at his chin. An empty champagne bottle stands at the BOTTOM left on the deal, and the stone steps rise in shadow at the LEFT edge toward the closed kitchen door.
shots.end: The narrator's face in the RIGHT third turned toward the stone steps, the cigar ember glowing at his chin, a curl of smoke rising through the amber light at the TOP, the empty bottle at the BOTTOM left.
source: I remember he wound up with my health, proposed in a speech of small variety and considerable intermittence.
I took a cigar, and went upstairs
shots.turn: a toasted guest -> drawn upstairs alone
shots.why: After the rambling toast to his health, the narrator takes a cigar and leaves the host to his bottle.

shots.frame: Wide of the roof at night, the narrator (grey eyes, battered brown felt hat) standing at the brick parapet, the London valley black beyond, the violet glow of the red weed at its centre and the fires of Kensington at the right.
shots.motion: The camera pans from the narrator at the parapet across to the violet glow of the red weed across the whole shot; the night breeze stirs the violet glow; the red fires flicker beyond Kensington.
shots.camera: Standing on the lead flat beside the dormer roof door, head height, six yards behind him, a 28mm lens; red firelight from Kensington comes from the RIGHT.
shots.at_rest: THE FOCUS OF THE PICTURE IS the narrator at the brick parapet in the LEFT third, his body a third of the frame's height, a cigar glowing in his hand. The pale violet glow streaks the black valley at CENTRE, the red fires flicker in the RIGHT third, and Mars burns red in the TOP left quarter.
shots.end: The violet glow of the red weed fills the CENTRE over the black valley, the red fires in the RIGHT third, the parapet along the BOTTOM third, the narrator's shoulder at the LEFT edge.

sounds.sound: distant fires crackling across the valley

source: At first I stared unintelligently across the London valley.
a pale, violet-purple fluorescent glow, quivering under the night breeze
I glanced from that to Mars, red and clear, glowing high in the west
shots.turn: idle stare -> wonder awake again
shots.why: The red weed's glow and Mars above it restore his sense of the proportion of things.

shots.frame: Close of the narrator (grey eyes, sixteen days of grey-brown beard) at the brick parapet, his face lit red from Kensington, staring toward the northern hills.
shots.motion: The camera pushes in toward the narrator's face at CENTRE; his jaw sets hard; his right arm swings back past his shoulder with the cigar.
shots.camera: Standing on the lead flat a yard to his right, eye height, an 85mm lens; red firelight falls from the RIGHT, deep black on the left of his face.
shots.at_rest: THE FOCUS OF THE PICTURE IS the narrator's face at CENTRE, his head half the frame's height, red firelight on his right cheek and deep black shadow on the LEFT side. The cigar glows in his hand at the BOTTOM edge, and the black valley fills the TOP right behind him with a faint violet haze.
shots.end: The narrator's face fills the frame from the TOP edge to the BOTTOM, his head two thirds of its height, the jaw set, his cigar arm swung back at the RIGHT edge, deep black shadow on the LEFT.
source: I seemed a traitor to my wife and to my kind; I was filled with remorse.
I resolved to leave this strange undisciplined dreamer of great things to his drink and gluttony, and to go on into London.
shots.turn: a day of folly -> resolve to go on into London
shots.why: Remorse names the day's purpose a dream; his own purpose is his wife and his kind, in London.

shots.frame: Insert from a high angle of the flung cigar lying on the lead flat at the foot of the brick parapet, its ember glowing.
shots.motion: The camera tracks sideways to the right past the corner of slate across the whole shot, with the flung cigar behind it; the night breeze blows sparks off the ember; the sparks drift along the grey lead.
shots.camera: A high angle looking down from above the parapet's coping, two feet off, a 50mm lens; red firelight comes from the RIGHT.
shots.at_rest: THE FOCUS OF THE PICTURE IS the flung cigar at CENTRE on the grey lead, its ember glowing orange. The brick parapet's foot runs along the RIGHT edge, a slate's corner juts in at the TOP left, and the parapet's black shadow covers the BOTTOM third.
shots.end: The cigar lies in the LEFT third on the grey lead, its ember dimmer, a trail of sparks across the CENTRE, the parapet's foot along the RIGHT edge in deep black shadow.
source: I remember I flung away the cigar with a certain wasteful symbolism.
shots.turn: comfort in his hand -> thrown away
shots.why: A wasteful, deliberate symbol: the holiday is over, held as a silent shot, a beat with no voice over it.

shots.frame: Wide of the narrator (grey eyes, battered brown felt hat) standing alone at the brick parapet as the late moon rises over the black London valley.
shots.motion: The camera rises above the narrator at the parapet across the whole shot, looking down over the black London valley to the violet glow; the narrator turns his face toward London; the late moon climbs above the northern hills.
shots.camera: Standing on the lead flat by the dormer roof door, chest height, eight yards behind him, a 28mm lens; the rising moon throws pale light from the RIGHT.
shots.at_rest: THE FOCUS OF THE PICTURE IS the narrator at the brick parapet at CENTRE, his body a quarter of the frame's height, facing the valley. The dormer roof door stands at the LEFT edge, the violet glow streaks the valley beyond the parapet, and Mars burns red in the TOP left quarter.
shots.end: High wide over the roof: the narrator small at the parapet at the BOTTOM centre facing London, the violet glow wide across the CENTRE of the black valley, the late moon low at the RIGHT, Mars at the TOP left.
source: I was still upon the roof when the late moon rose.
shots.turn: the soldier's follower -> his own man again
shots.why: The world answers with the late moon over a dark London: the way on lies there, alone.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: That night I hid in the inn on Putney Hill, and lit no lamp for fear of them.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: The house was stripped already. A rat had left me a crust and two pineapple tins.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: Let the Heat-Ray have struck her painlessly out of being.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: At dawn I crept out like a rat from its hole, pockets full of biscuits.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: The road was strewn with wreckage from the flight. I reached the common, lonelier than ever.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: Frogs swarmed in a marsh, stubborn to live, and I stopped to learn from them.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: Then I felt watched. Something crouching in the bushes rose up, a man with a cutlass.

lines.speaker: artilleryman
lines.text: Stop! Where do you come from?

lines.speaker: artilleryman
lines.text: They've built a flying-machine, and are learning to fly.

lines.speaker: artilleryman
lines.text: Aren't you satisfied it is up with humanity? We're beat.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: I hunted for an answer and found none. To them we were ants, and eatable.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: I watched the beaten soldier's hand sweep across London, and something in me stirred.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: Great God! But you are a man indeed!

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: His week of digging was a hole I could cut in a day. Still, I dug gladly.

lines.speaker: artilleryman
lines.text: I am host today. Champagne! Let us take a rest.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: By lamplight I won three hard chess games from him, and learned his poker besides.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: So we played cards for London, parish by parish, and I found it delightful.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: Late in the night he toasted my health. I took a cigar and climbed upstairs.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: Under Mars and the violet weed-glow, I resolved to leave the dreamer and go on into London.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: The day's folly burned in me. I had betrayed my wife and my kind.

lines.speaker: artilleryman
lines.text: And man has come back to his own.
